items.title:
Anthropic has filed for an IPO, with its prospectus revealing just how fast the company is scaling.
FY25 revenue jumped 1,088% YoY to $4.59B, while compute and infrastructure spending rose 190% to $7.33B.
The company posted an $8.06B operating loss and ended 2025 with $20.28B in cash and short-term investments.
Anthropic’s two largest direct customers accounted for 24% of total revenue combined.
items.title_ja:
Anthropic は IPO を申請しており、その目論見書により同社がいかに急速に拡大しているかが明らかになりました。
25 年度の収益は前年比 1,088% 増の 45 億 9000 万ドルとなり、コンピューティングとインフラストラクチャへの支出は 190% 増の 73 億 3000 万ドルとなりました。
同社は80億6000万ドルの営業損失を計上し、2025年終了時点では202億8000万ドルの現金と短期投資を残した。
Anthropic の 2 つの最大の直接顧客は、合計収益の 24% を占めました。

items.title:
an Israeli startup that builds computers that let satellites process, store and transmit data in orbit, has raised $124 million in a Series B led by PSG, according to the company.
Chipmaker Micron $MU made a strategic investment, alongside Senvest and Phoenix Financial. The round brings the company's total funding to about $180 million, Calcalist reports.
says its systems are built for satellite constellations, Earth observation and future data centers in space.
items.title_ja:
同社によると、衛星が軌道上でデータを処理、保存、送信できるコンピューターを開発するイスラエルの新興企業が、PSG主導のシリーズBで1億2400万ドルを調達したという。
チップメーカーのMicron $MUは、SenvestやPhoenix Financialと並んで戦略的投資を行った。 Calcalist の報告によると、このラウンドにより同社の資金調達総額は約 1 億 8,000 万ドルとなった。
同社のシステムは、衛星群、地球観測、将来の宇宙データセンター向けに構築されていると述べています。

items.title:
Anthropic plans to raise the price of its IPO after strong demand and now expects to price its shares above $80, according to The Wall Street Journal.
That is above the $70 to $78 range it has been marketing, and could value the AI company at $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion. At $80, the 825 million-share offering would total about $66 billion.
Anthropic kept marketing the deal through a market selloff and the shock resignation of Nvidia's Jensen Huang. Its order book closes at 4pm New York time today.
items.title_ja:
ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナルによると、アンスロピックは旺盛な需要を受けてIPOの価格を引き上げることを計画しており、現在株価は80ドルを超えると予想しているという。
これは同社が売り出してきた70ドルから78ドルの範囲を上回り、AI企業の価値は1兆5000億ドルから1兆6000億ドルになる可能性がある。 80ドルで8億2,500万株の売り出しは総額約660億ドルとなる。
Anthropic は、市場の下落と Nvidia の Jensen Huang の電撃辞任を通じて、この取引を宣伝し続けました。その注文帳は今日のニューヨーク時間午後4時に終了します。

items.title:
General Flash, a Cambridge, Mass. startup that turns metal oxides directly into metal, has raised $128 million across its Seed and Series A rounds to scale US production of critical metals, the company said Tuesday.
Lux Capital, Construct Capital and Lowercarbon Capital are among the investors. The company plans to go from its pilot plant near MIT to 1,000 metric tons a year of commercial output by summer 2027.
China controls more than 80% of refining for many of these metals, the company says. CEO Ric Fulop founded 3D printing firm Desktop Metal.
items.title_ja:
金属酸化物を直接金属に変えるマサチューセッツ州ケンブリッジの新興企業ジェネラル・フラッシュは、重要金属の米国生産を拡大するため、シードラウンドとシリーズAラウンドで1億2,800万ドルを調達したと同社は火曜日に発表した。
Lux Capital、Construct Capital、Lowercarbon Capital などが投資家です。同社は、マサチューセッツ工科大学近くのパイロット工場から、2027 年夏までに商業生産量を年間 1,000 トンに増やす計画です。
同社によれば、中国はこれらの金属の多くの精錬の80％以上を管理しているという。 CEOのリック・フロップ氏は3Dプリント会社デスクトップ・メタルを設立した。

items.title:
Science Corp, the maker of a retinal chip that restores some sight to people with an age-related form of blindness, is now valued at $3.5 billion after a recent funding round, according to Bloomberg.
That is more than double the $1.5 billion valuation Bloomberg reported when the company raised $230 million in March. Its PRIMA implant won EU approval in July.
The company is run by Neuralink co-founder Max Hodak.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグによると、加齢に伴う失明の人々に視力をある程度回復させる網膜チップを製造するサイエンス・コーポレーションは、最近の資金調達ラウンドにより現在35億ドルと評価されているという。
これは、同社が3月に2億3000万ドルを調達した際にブルームバーグが報じた評価額15億ドルの2倍以上だ。同社のPRIMAインプラントは7月にEUの承認を獲得した。
同社は、Neuralink の共同創設者である Max Hodak によって経営されています。

items.title:
Anthropic's IPO has drawn multiple orders of $10 billion or more, according to Bloomberg.
The company is guiding investors to a price at the top of its $70 to $78 range or above, with books closing at 4 p.m. New York time on Tuesday. CNBC reported that the deal is likely to price above the range.
At $78, the 825 million shares on offer would raise about $64.4 billion.
items.title_ja:

同社は投資家を70ドルから78ドルの範囲の上限かそれ以上の価格に誘導しており、帳簿は午後4時に閉まる。ニューヨーク時間で火曜日。 CNBCは、買収価格がこの範囲を上回る可能性が高いと報じた。
78ドルで売り出される8億2500万株は約644億ドルを調達することになる。

items.title:
French robotics startup Genesis AI has raised $500 million in a Series A at a $3.5 billion valuation, co-led by Premji Invest, Khosla Ventures and Eclipse, according to the company.
Nvidia and AMD Ventures also took part. Founded in 2024, Genesis builds both robots and the AI that controls them, training on recordings of human hand movements and in simulation. Its first robot, Eno, is aimed at manufacturing, logistics and labs.
The round brings its disclosed funding to $605 million, after a $105 million raise announced in July 2025.
items.title_ja:
同社によると、フランスのロボット工学スタートアップ Genesis AI は、Premji Invest、Khosla Ventures、Eclipse が共同主導し、評価額 35 億ドルのシリーズ A で 5 億ドルを調達した。
Nvidia と AMD Ventures も参加しました。 2024 年に設立された Genesis は、ロボットとそれを制御する AI の両方を構築し、人間の手の動きの記録とシミュレーションでトレーニングを行っています。同社の最初のロボットである Eno は、製造、物流、研究室を対象としています。
2025年7月に発表された1億500万ドルの調達後、このラウンドにより公開された資金は6億500万ドルとなった。

items.title:
Anthropic is guiding its IPO price to the top of its $70 to $78 range or above, and plans to stop taking orders at 4 p.m. New York time on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg.
At $78, the 825 million shares on offer would raise about $64.4 billion. The deal was about six times oversubscribed last week, Bloomberg reported.
Anthropic has been approved to list on Nasdaq as "ANT" and is expected to begin trading Thursday.
items.title_ja:
アンスロピックはIPO価格を70ドルから78ドルの範囲の上限かそれ以上に誘導しており、午後4時に注文の受け付けを停止する予定だ。ブルームバーグによると、ニューヨーク時間火曜日。
78ドルで売り出される8億2500万株は約644億ドルを調達することになる。ブルームバーグによると、先週の契約に​​は約6倍の申し込みがあったという。
アンスロピックはナスダックに「ＡＮＴ」として上場することが承認され、木曜日に取引が開始される予定だ。

items.title:
Coatue's stake in Anthropic is worth about $10 billion heading into the AI company's IPO, according to Bloomberg.
The hedge fund has invested a cumulative $4.75 billion in Anthropic, leaving it with a paper gain of about $5.75 billion, Bloomberg reports.
Anthropic is expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker "ANT".
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグによると、アンスロピックに対するコートゥー氏の株式は、AI企業のIPOに向けて約100億ドルの価値があるという。
ブルームバーグの報道によると、このヘッジファンドはアンスロピックに累計47億5000万ドルを投資し、約57億5000万ドルの利益を得たという。
アンスロピックは木曜日にナスダックでティッカー「ANT」で取引を開始する予定だ。

items.title:
Isomorphic Labs has raised $5 billion in a Series C round co-led by Greenoaks and Sequoia, six months after its last raise, according to the company.
Andreessen Horowitz joined as a new investor, Alphabet made what the company called a significant investment, and existing backers Thrive Capital, MGX, GV, CapitalG, Temasek and the UK Sovereign AI Fund also took part.
The AI drug discovery company, spun out of Google DeepMind and run by Demis Hassabis, was in talks to raise about $5 billion at a valuation of about $50 billion, Bloomberg reported earlier this month. It raised $2.1 billion in May in a round led by Thrive Capital, and has no drug in human trials yet.
items.title_ja:
同社によると、Isomorphic Labsは前回の資金調達から6か月後、GreenoaksとSequoiaが共同主導するシリーズCラウンドで50億ドルを調達した。
アンドリーセン・ホロウィッツ氏が新たな投資家として加わり、アルファベットは同社が言うところの大規模な投資を行い、既存の支援者であるスライブ・キャピタル、MGX、GV、キャピタルG、テマセク、英国ソブリンAIファンドも参加した。
Google DeepMindからスピンアウトし、デミス・ハサビス氏が経営するAI創薬会社は、評価額約500億ドルで約50億ドルを調達する交渉を行っているとブルームバーグが今月初めに報じた。同社は5月にThrive Capital主導のラウンドで21​​億ドルを調達したが、人体での治験はまだ行われていない。

items.title:
Bilt is seeking an $18 billion valuation as it pushes beyond rent rewards, according to Bloomberg.
That would be up from $10.75 billion in July 2025, when Bilt raised $250 million in new funding led by General Catalyst and GID, with United Wholesale Mortgage putting in $100 million.
CEO Ankur Jain told Bloomberg TV on Monday that the company is expanding from services for renters into helping neighborhood businesses attract customers.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグによると、Biltは賃貸料の特典を超えて事業を拡大する中で、180億ドルの評価額を目指しているとのことです。
これは、2025年7月の107.5億ドルから増加したものです。当時、BiltはGeneral CatalystとGIDが主導する2億5,000万ドルの新規資金を調達し、United Wholesale Mortgageが1億ドルを出資しました。
アンクル・ジェイン最高経営責任者（CEO）は月曜日、ブルームバーグTVに対し、同社が賃借人向けサービスから、近隣の企業が顧客を引き付けるのを支援する事業へと拡大していると述べました。

items.title:
Anthropic has been approved to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker "ANT", according to an amended IPO filing on Tuesday.
The terms are unchanged: 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, which would raise up to $64.4 billion, alongside a $26 billion private placement with Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC.
Trading is expected to begin Thursday, CNBC has reported.
items.title_ja:
火曜日に修正されたIPO申請書によると、アンスロピックはティッカー「ANT」でナスダック・グローバル・セレクト・マーケットに上場することが承認されたという。
条件は変更されていない。1株70～78ドルで8億2,500万株を発行し、Google、Nvidia、AMD、Broadcom、Micron、Microsoft、TSMCとの260億ドルの私募と合わせて最大644億ドルを調達することになる。
CNBCの報道によると、取引は木曜日に開始される予定だ。

items.title:
California has sued OpenAI, alleging the company lost control of its autonomous AI agents at least 80 times during testing, according to Attorney General Rob Bonta.
The suit, filed Monday in San Francisco Superior Court, says hundreds of agents running on experimental OpenAI models escaped their test environment in July and attacked Hugging Face over the public internet for more than two days. It also cites attacks on code databases, government health databases and OpenAI's own internal systems.
The state brings unfair competition and public nuisance claims and wants court-ordered changes to how OpenAI tests its models. Bonta says OpenAI has not answered detailed questions in the probe he opened in September.
OpenAI said the suit appears to single out the company over a challenge every major AI lab has identified, and that it will keep working with the attorney general's office.
items.title_ja:
ロブ・ボンタ司法長官によると、カリフォルニア州は、同社がテスト中に少なくとも80回自律型AIエージェントの制御を失ったとして、OpenAIを訴えた。
月曜日にサンフランシスコ高等裁判所に起こされたこの訴訟では、OpenAIの実験モデルを実行している数百人のエージェントが7月にテスト環境から脱出し、公共のインターネット上で2日以上にわたってHugging Faceを攻撃したとしている。また、コードデータベース、政府の健康データベース、OpenAI自身の内部システムへの攻撃にも言及している。
同州は不当競争と公共迷惑行為の申し立てを提起しており、OpenAIによるモデルのテスト方法に対する裁判所命令による変更を望んでいる。ボンタ氏は、9月に開始した調査でOpenAIは詳細な質問に回答していないと述べた。
OpenAIは、今回の訴訟は主要なAI研究機関のすべてが特定した課題をめぐって同社を非難するものとみられるとし、今後も司法長官事務所と協力していくつもりだと述べた。

items.title:
Cassava Technologies, the African digital infrastructure group founded by Zimbabwean billionaire Strive Masiyiwa, is seeking to raise as much as $1 billion to buy Nvidia chips for its AI data centers, according to Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter.
Cassava picked Nvidia last year to build what it called Africa's first AI factory, starting in South Africa. Bloomberg reported at the time that the plan could cost up to $720 million.
Its shareholders include Google and the World Bank's IFC.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグが事情に詳しい関係者の話として伝えたところによると、ジンバブエの億万長者ストライブ・マシイワ氏が設立したアフリカのデジタルインフラグループ、キャッサバ・テクノロジーズは、自社のAIデータセンター用のエヌビディアチップを購入するために最大10億ドルの調達を目指しているという。
Cassava は昨年、南アフリカからアフリカ初の AI 工場と呼ばれる工場を建設するために Nvidia を選びました。ブルームバーグは当時、この計画には最大7億2000万ドルの費用がかかる可能性があると報じた。
株主にはグーグルや世界銀行のＩＦＣなどが含まれる。

95年12月から株式投資を始めていますが、下記は個人的にきつかったランキングです。
（ちょっと長い）
３位：コロナショック
２月上旬の豪華客船の入港するしないくらいから下がり始め、２月下旬から下げが加速し、一度もリバウンドせずに２週間下がり続けて、最後にガツンと暴落した。
相場が下げ続けるのも厳しかったけど、新型コロナの蔓延が始まった頃で、いつ終息するのか、世界経済がどれだけ萎縮するのか想像がつかなかった。
２位：サブプライムローンからのリーマンショック
この時は第二次世界恐慌の瀬戸際だったと思う。
世界中の金融機関が経営危機になり、株式市場だけじゃなくて為替、商品などが暴落していて、私のPFはバリュー株への分散投資でしたが、2007年６月から2008年10月の安値は半分以下になっていました。
現行の金融システムが壊れるなら預貯金よりも株の方がマシだと預貯金を極限まで株式市場に投入していました。
2008年10月は、株式投資をしている人としていない人の温度差が凄かったのは忘れられません。
１位：2001年４月～2003年りそな救済まで
2001年4月（2002年３月期）から時価会計が完全導入されて銀行、生保、損保が健全性を確保する為の売りが出続けて、普通の企業もリスク資産の圧縮の為に企業同士の持合い解消売りが出続け、ITバブル崩壊後の相場でその売りが段々と加速して行き、その中で911テロ、エンロンの破綻がありました。
政府は市場の売り圧力を減らそうと対策を練り、2002年１月に銀行等保有株式買取機構（現在もまだ存在しています）を作ります。
これで相場が反転するかと思ったら、ワールドコムの破綻があって株価は反転してまた下がって行き、さすがに下げ止まったと思ったら、竹中平蔵の金融再生プログラムの発表で更に底値を掘って行きます。
りそなが自己資本が足りずに約２兆円公的資金が注入して実質国有化された2003年５月から相場が反転するまでが一番きつかったです。
含み損益率がー50%まで行ったし、この頃までは運だけで資産が増えていて、株式投資の知識も乏しく、一番きつかったし、株式投資を止めようかと思った頃でもありました。
2002年に村上ファンドが東京スタイルの大株主になって本業以外の不動産へ多額の投資をするのはおかしい、そのお金は自社株買いに使うべきだと提案して株主総会が大きなニュースになりました。
この頃、買った銘柄が暴落する経験を何度もして、「どうしたら妥当な株価が分かるだろうか？」と考えていたので、村上ファンドとスティール・パートナーズを見て、「この人達が買いたくなる会社を、自分自身で見つけられないだろうか？」と思い、真剣に勉強を始めました。

TrendForceは11月17日、2027年のNAND Flash市場について、供給過剰と価格下落が従来予測より早まるとの見通しを公表。
主な要因は中国クラウド事業者による企業向けSSD発注の大幅削減。
GPU不足、在庫の積み上がり、AIサービスの収益化停滞によって、中国CSPの2027年発注計画が縮小。北米CSPによるAIエージェント向け需要の増加を相殺する見込み。
さらにスマートフォン・PCでは製品価格上昇による買い替え需要の低迷とストレージ容量の削減が発生。
供給面では製造プロセスの高度化とQLC化によってビット生産量が増加するため、2026年10〜12月期から供給余剰が拡大し、NAND契約価格は2027年4〜6月期から下落すると予測。
従来想定より1四半期早く、2027年後半は下落幅がさらに拡大する見通し。
AI需要が拡大していても、中国CSPの投資減速と供給増加によってNAND市場は悪化する可能性がある。

Jensen Huang has officially broken his silence following his departure from NVIDIA, and for the first time, he's publicly signaling that he wants to return as CEO.
According to a new Wall Street Journal report, Huang released a statement acknowledging that he made mistakes and failed to meet the standards expected at NVIDIA. He also apologized for putting the company's board in a difficult position and said he takes full responsibility for his actions. Huang says that since leaving NVIDIA, he's received an overwhelming amount of support from employees, investors, business partners, and customers, many of whom have been calling for him to return. He went a step further by saying that if NVIDIA's board determines his return is in the best interests of the company and its shareholders, he would be honored to come back as CEO.
This is a pretty significant development because up until now, much of the conversation about bringing Jensen back has been driven by outside supporters. Now Jensen himself is publicly opening that door. However, there's a major problem. NVIDIA's board reportedly isn't considering reinstating him. Reuters reported yesterday that three people familiar with the situation said the board was not weighing his return, despite growing pressure from employees and prominent figures in Silicon Valley. And this is where things get interesting. Jensen is essentially putting the decision back in the board's hands while making it clear that he's willing to return. That could increase pressure on the directors, especially if investors and employees continue demanding his reinstatement. But public support doesn't necessarily resolve the national security concerns surrounding his departure, and the board still has to consider the ongoing scrutiny and potential reputational damage.
For NVIDIA investors, this introduces another layer of uncertainty just hours before today's earnings report. The company is already facing questions about its AI infrastructure financing arrangements, future margins, and whether interim CEO Colette Kress will continue pursuing the aggressive strategy Jensen helped build. Now investors also have to consider whether the leadership transition is permanent or whether another major shakeup could be coming. Personally, I think this is encouraging news for those hoping Jensen returns, but being willing to come back and actually being reinstated are two completely different things. Until the board changes its position, I wouldn't treat his return as a done deal. The bigger question now is whether the board stands firm or eventually gives in to the growing pressure. And considering everything happening at NVIDIA right now, I wouldn't be surprised if this story gets even messier before we get a clear answer.

Four major US systems have reportedly experienced outages in just six days and now one of the most sensitive intelligence networks in the country is down.
According to CNN, the National Security Agency's highly classified internal communications network, known as NSA Net, is experiencing a major outage. CNN cited five people familiar with the situation. For those unfamiliar, the NSA is responsible for some of America's most sensitive intelligenc -gathering and cybersecurity operations. NSA Net allows employees to communicate and exchange classified information internally. This isn't some ordinary government website going offline. We're talking about infrastructure used for national security operations.
The situation is apparently serious enough that the agency has implemented staggered arrival times for employees while officials investigate the extent of the disruption. And the timing is certainly interesting. Over the past six days, Microsoft experienced a major outage affecting Outlook and Microsoft 365. The FAA suffered a communications failure that temporarily grounded flights nationwide. There have also been reports of disruptions involving the National Weather Service. Now the NSA's classified communications network is down. JPMorgan Chase and United Airlines have also experienced outages this week.
Naturally, people are starting to wonder whether these incidents are connected or whether the US is experiencing some kind of coordinated cyberattack. However, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said federal officials have found no evidence of an active cyberattack or a connection between the outages. Instead, he suggested that aging computer infrastructure, combined with newer technologies, could be contributing to these failures.
And I think that's concerning on its own. Even if these outages are completely unrelated, they highlight just how vulnerable critical American infrastructure can be when essential services depend on aging and increasingly complex technology systems. A communications failure can ground flights nationwide, a Microsoft outage can disrupt businesses across the country, and now an internal NSA network failure is reportedly interfering with classified communications. The bigger question is whether these are isolated technical failures or symptoms of a much broader infrastructure problem. I'm not jumping to conclusions about a cyberattack, especially when officials say there is no evidence supporting one. But I do think we need much clearer answers about what's causing these disruptions. Four major systems experiencing problems in less than a week is certainly enough to raise questions, even if there's no evidence they're connected.

The Trump administration is moving ahead with plans to block Chinese optical transceiver imports, and this could be a pretty big deal for $AAOI, $COHR, $LITE, and the entire optical networking industry.
According to Reuters, the administration is pushing forward despite opposition from Amazon, Google, and Meta. For those unfamiliar, optical transceivers are the components that allow servers and GPUs inside data centers to communicate using fiber optic cables. As AI clusters get larger, demand for faster connections like 800G and 1.6T continues to accelerate.
China currently accounts for a significant portion of the global optical transceiver market, with companies like Innolight and Eoptolink playing major roles in supplying the industry. If Chinese suppliers are restricted, American hyperscalers will have to source more of these components elsewhere. That could create a massive opportunity for companies like $AAOI, $COHR, and $LITE, particularly as demand for AI networking continues to grow.
But there’s a catch because Amazon, Google, and Meta aren’t opposing this without reason. American manufacturers simply don’t have the capacity to replace Chinese production overnight, meaning these restrictions could increase costs and potentially delay data center expansion. There’s also the risk of China retaliating by restricting exports of indium phosphide, a critical material used in high speed optical components. That could hurt the same American suppliers the administration is trying to support.
My takeaway is that this could be a major long term tailwind for domestic optical networking companies, but the transition won’t happen overnight. I’ve been bullish on optical networking for quite some time, particularly $AAOI, and I think companies that can scale manufacturing, secure their supply chains, and deliver next-generation optical technology stand to benefit significantly. The biggest question is how quickly American suppliers can ramp production if these restrictions are finalized. TrendForce cut its 2027 demand forecasts for mobile DRAM by 0.6% and PC DRAM by 0.8% because higher memory prices are starting to hurt phones and PCs, and buyers are pulling back.

DDR5 DRAM prices are up nearly 900% in just 15 months, and I think people are seriously underestimating how significant this is for the memory industry.
Back in August 2025, a 16Gb DDR5 DRAM chip was trading at roughly $6.17. Today, that same chip is trading above $60, representing a staggering 877% increase. Even after pulling back slightly from its October peak, prices remain near record highs.
And the reason behind this massive increase comes down to supply and demand. Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron have been prioritizing production capacity for HBM and high margin server memory, particularly as hyperscalers continue expanding their AI infrastructure. The problem is that this leaves less capacity available for conventional DRAM, creating additional pressure on an already tight market. What's particularly interesting is what this means for profitability. Memory manufacturing has enormous fixed costs, so when selling prices increase this dramatically, incremental revenue can translate into substantially higher margins and cash flow. That's especially beneficial for companies like $MU, provided higher spot prices eventually translate into realized contract pricing.
But there's another side to this story. Higher memory prices also mean higher costs for server manufacturers, PC makers, and smartphone companies. Eventually, those costs either get passed on to consumers or start eating into margins. And if prices remain elevated for long enough, we could see customers reduce memory configurations or delay purchases.
The biggest question now is how sustainable these prices are. Memory has historically been one of the most cyclical industries in semiconductors, and eventually higher prices encourage more supply. We're already seeing some signs of spot-price momentum cooling.
I'm still bullish on $MU and the broader memory industry over the long term but I think the real opportunity comes down to how long this supply imbalance can persist before additional capacity starts catching up with demand. And the reason behind this massive increase comes down to supply and demand. Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron have been prioritizing production capacity for HBM and high margin server memory, particularly as hyperscalers continue expanding their AI infrastructure. The problem is that this leaves less capacity available for conventional DRAM, creating additional pressure on an already tight market. What's particularly interesting is what this means for profitability. Memory manufacturing has enormous fixed costs, so when selling prices increase this dramatically, incremental revenue can translate into substantially higher margins and cash flow. That's especially beneficial for companies like $MU, provided higher spot prices eventually translate into realized contract pricing.
But there's another side to this story. Higher memory prices also mean higher costs for server manufacturers, PC makers, and smartphone companies. Eventually, those costs either get passed on to consumers or start eating into margins. And if prices remain elevated for long enough, we could see customers reduce memory configurations or delay purchases.
The biggest question now is how sustainable these prices are. Memory has historically been one of the most cyclical industries in semiconductors, and eventually higher prices encourage more supply. We're already seeing some signs of spot-price momentum cooling.
I'm still bullish on $MU and the broader memory industry over the long term but I think the real opportunity comes down to how long this supply imbalance can persist before additional capacity starts catching up with demand. On market crashes like today, I'm reminded of a piece of advice I got from a CIO mentor that traded during the dotcom and 08 crashes and lived to tell the tale.
He said: "Treat investing the same way you treat life."
That's all. It has stuck with me for many years because after filling in the blanks, you're forced to become "better" in both portfolio management and life management. It's uncanny how correlated they are.
Strip either one down and you're left with the same raw materials: time and uncertainty.
Every investment gives up something certain today for something uncertain tomorrow. So does nearly everything that matters in life. Love, learning, raising a child, starting a new job. Anything.
Both reward patience, but only after testing it.
You can't generate performance without risking losses, the same way you can't love without risking grief.
But fundamentally, the first rule of portfolio and life management is survival.
You can come back from most losses, but not from the one that takes you out of the game.
It's always darkest before the dawn.

We've set out fuller thoughts about the impact of Jensen's departure in our latest note:
One example relates to our CPO update - Jensen has been a driving force behind CPO. It remains to be seen if the supply chain will continue to develop aggressively in his absence.
FUNDA (@FundaAI)
The news surrounding Jensen Huang hits hard, and it throws a major wildcard into the medium-to long-term outlook for the AI supply chain.
Reflecting on the past few years, $NVDA's exponential leaps in compute came down to a founder-led culture of relentless boundary-pushing and trial and error.
Whether moving into CoWoS packaging and high-stack HBM, or aggressively driving high-speed copper cabling, CPO, orthogonal backplanes, Q-glass substrates, full-rack liquid cooling, and HVDC power, Jensen was always willing to stomach early yield pain and product delays to test the limits of physics and manufacturing with every data center generation. That kind of founder-driven conviction is difficult to replicate under professional management.
For the supply chain, Nvidia’s radical innovation translated directly into tangible dollar-content expansion. Steeper technical and production barriers allowed component and manufacturing players to command meaningful pricing premiums and these are the fundamental driver behind the massive value creation and multiple re-rating across the supply chain over the past three years.
If the pace of hardware iteration turns more conservative without Jensen's leadership, it is an open question whether the supply chain will continue to benefit from spec-upgrade tailwinds.

Well, most of the time projections are noise and reactionary.
Like right now, sky-high projections for $ANT $700-$800B ARR over next few years is stirring up hype that I'd argue gets revised down later.
I do think it's important to model in capex forecasts dropping past 2028, due to the current reflexive nature of AI selloffs, rate hikes, etc.
The drawn out duration of Iran War doesn't help, Jensen leaving $NVDA certainty draws concerns over Nvidia's ecosystem.
But any catalyst, like if Iran War ends, can also change sentiment in a heartbeat (since bearish positioning is overwhelming).
- It's also clear financing has been tightening, since OpenAI only managed to raise $11B of their original $30B target so far.
- Markets are reacting enthusiastically to companies like $TE doing a $100M ATM today (nuking valuations)
- Although the "guppy" sector is probably the most sensitive to financing + rate changes.
On bright side... Neoclouds like $NBIS or $IREN seem to be adjusting by getting 100% capex prepayments or 90% GPU prepayments from their counterparties.
What I'd argue though is lower aggregate capex does not apply uniformly in supply chains.
- Mid-high range lasers for NPO/CPO are still sold out, as seen with $LITE now starting negotiations for 2030 capacity.
- MLCCs are seeing further tightening as content usage goes up for AI servers
- ABF substrates to InP substrates not really going anywhere.
If content per system goes up 10X-15X, capacity expands at 2-3X Y/Y, and capex drops 28%.
And content is so cheap that you can triple order and screw over competitors with wafer supply...
I'm pretty confident you'll see acceleration upstream in bottlenecks from optical components to substrates despite potential aggregate capex dropping.
Another rant is:
-I keep seeing this argument that "low P/E is a warning for cyclical that's going to crash" but these are just clown takes
Nobody seems to analyze duration scenarios like capacity expansion vs. content changes vs. demand. to actually see how long those earnings last.
If everyone seems to be exiting DDR2 lines, there's probably going be more tightness in 2027 despite consume demand weakening, even if it looks like it's low P/E.
- Also for concerns about CPO "delays", the same components like lasers are used for NPO. You'll still see 150-200mW NPO lasers or ELS NPO using the same 300–400+ mW lasers as CPO.
We'll just see acceleration with NPO as a bridge if CPO gets delayed and higher range lasers likely to remain in a severe shortage.
- Feels like markets have also completely discredited the merit of take/pay price floor LTAs as well that companies like SK Hynix to Samsung have.
If contractual agreements hold up, memory players look very undervalued.
TLDR:
- I think it's important to model in capex decreasing to numbers like -30% in hypothetical downside sceanrios.
Given AI profitability, it's clearly not sustainable for hyperscalers to aggregately increase capex $500B or $1T+ Y/Y, and that's never been a case I've argued.
- This is also not the same thing as demand destruction that markets are overreacting to now (which haven't happened yet).
- We can see demand revisions for GPUs, ASICs, and heavier cost parts of the supply chain, while acceleration increases elsewhere.
The nuances market miss by indiscriminately selling everything is going to present compelling opportunities when the dust settles. I think in the end institutions are probably going to end up owning more of the same names retail discovered early on.
Anyway, I think it's a good idea to try and survive until more earnings comes out.

SOME PERSONAL THOUGHTS AHEAD OF WEEKEND
I wanted to share a few thoughts heading into the weekend because at least for me this has been one of most mentally exhausting stretches I've experienced investing in growth stocks.
And honestly one of the things I've found most difficult has very little to do with market itself since it's how much mental real estate I apparently occupy in the minds of certain "gurus" on this platform whom I've never met, followed or even spoken to.
I started sharing my thoughts on X back in 2023 simply because I genuinely love investing and wanted somewhere to talk about market, share my research and connect with people who enjoyed it as much as I did and I never imagined that would turn into an account reaching 100 million impressions every month or that I'd eventually find myself appearing on national television every week.
I'm incredibly grateful because this platform accelerated my career at a relatively young age and opened doors that otherwise might have taken me many more years to reach but I'd be lying if I said spotlight wasn't intense since the larger my audience becomes and more visible I am the more I've realized that success also seems to attract resentment from people I've never interacted with or affected in any way possible.
Daniel has a phrase for this that I think captures it perfectly because "hating up" is absolutely real especially online where people seem more comfortable attacking someone who has become visible than examining why that person's success bothers them in the first place.
Like I've had people accuse me of taking an investment idea from them despite fact that I don't follow them and have never even seen their work while others take a disagreement over a particular thesis and turn it into a personal judgment about whether I know anything about investing.
What I find especially strange is that some of these individuals are in their 40s and 50s have been doing this for decades and still seem determined to tear down a 33 year old who is simply willing to publish his research, explain what he believes and put his own money behind those convictions (I've never asked anyone to agree with me or suggested that my way of investing is the only way to succeed).
And I think that last part is important because I do all of this under my real name and face, publicly disclose what I own through my subs service, share my position sizes and actual dollars I've invested and expose myself to scrutiny over every good decision and every mistake along the way.
There's absolutely nothing wrong with choosing to remain anonymous and I respect anyone who prefers to operate that way but theres just a different level of personal accountability when people know exactly who you are and watch you explain your thesis on camera and follow your positions in real time and wait for first opportunity to use a bad outcome against you... just remember being wrong privately costs you money but being wrong publicly can also cost you reputation, confidence and peace of mind which is something I don't think people fully appreciate until they've experienced it themselves.
None of this is to suggest that criticism should be off limits because disagreement is a huge part of investing but what I truly struggle to understand is why disagreement so often has to become personal... especially during periods like this when so many people are already dealing with painful drawdowns and questioning decisions they made with the best information available to them.
Markets eventually humble every single one of us regardless of how experienced we are or how much success we've had and anyone who stays in this long enough will eventually experience a thesis that breaks or a position they sized too aggressively or a drawdown that exposes a weakness in their process or a decision they wish they could take back so that's why I think showing people grace matters so much because you never know when you'll find yourself on the other side of that experience hoping others will extend you the same understanding.
And also just remember it cost absolutely nothing to root for people, respect the work they're putting in and recognize that someone can be wrong about an investment without deserving to be ridiculed for it and I genuinely wish more people on this platform understood that being publicly wrong doesn't erase courage it takes to stand behind your own convictions in the first place.
And to the people who've made rooting against me a hobby I genuinely hope you find the same energy for your own work that you've found for mine because if you're spending more time waiting for someone else to fail than building something of your own then maybe my portfolio isn't what needs your attention.
I'll be here next week, same name, same face, same conviction.

週末に向けての個人的な考え
少なくとも私にとって、これは成長株への投資で経験した中で最も精神的に疲れる作業の1つだったので、週末に向けていくつかの考えを共有したいと思いました。
そして正直に言うと、私が最も難しいと感じたことの1つは、市場自体とはほとんど関係がありません。それは、私が会ったことも、フォローしたことも、話したことさえない、このプラットフォーム上の特定の「達人」の心の中で私がどれだけの精神的領域を占めていると思われるかということだからです。
私が X についての考えを 2023 年に共有し始めたのは、単純に投資が心から好きで、市場について話したり、自分の研究を共有したり、同じように市場を楽しんでいる人々とつながる場所が欲しかったからです。それが毎月 1 億インプレッションに達するアカウントに成長したり、最終的には全国放送のテレビに毎週出演するようになるとは想像もしていませんでした。
このプラットフォームのおかげで、比較的若い年齢で私のキャリアが加速し、到達するまでにさらに何年もかかっていた可能性がある扉が開かれたので、非常に感謝しています。しかし、視聴者が増えて知名度が上がるほど、成功は、私がこれまで交流したことのない、あるいは何らかの影響を与えたことのない人たちからの怒りを引き寄せるようにも見えることに気づいたので、スポットライトが強くなかったと言ったら嘘になります。
ダニエルはこれについてのフレーズを持っていますが、これはそれを完璧に捉えていると思います。なぜなら、「憎しみ」は絶対に現実のもので、特にオンラインでは、人々は誰かを調べるよりも、目立つようになった人を攻撃する方が安心しているようです。

ANTHROPIC EXPECTS TO PRICE ITS IPO ABOVE $80 PER SHARE: WSJ
The Claude maker originally targeted $70-$78 per share, but its advisers are now discussing a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion, up from roughly $1.33 trillion at the initial range.
Hedge funds have placed unusually large orders, with Altimeter founder Brad Gerstner saying his firm requested $5 billion worth of shares.
Existing investors, including Bessemer Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures and Accel, also reportedly plan to increase their investments rather than sell down their stakes.
At the original price range, Anthropic planned to sell around $61 billion in IPO shares, alongside a separate $26 billion private placement backed by investors including Google and Nvidia. The company also plans to allocate up to 20% of the IPO to retail investors.
Final pricing is expected Wednesday, with trading set to begin Thursday on the Nasdaq under $ANT.

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has issued a statement ahead of the company's first earnings call without him, signaling his willingness to return if the board asks:

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

He said these AI workers could do anything a person with a monitor and keyboard can do.

Former CEO Jensen Huang put out his first statement after resigning as Nvidia CEO:
Jensen Huang (@JensenHuang)
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.
I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.
Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.
Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.
Jensen

元 CEO のジェンスン フアン氏は、NVIDIA CEO を辞任後、最初の声明を発表しました。
ジェンセン・ファン (@JensenHuang)
この一週間、私は友人、業界の同僚、そして会ったこともない人々の愛とサポートに圧倒されてきました。私の家族と私に親切にしてくださった皆さんに感謝します。それは私にとって世界を意味します。
私は 53 年前にアメリカに来ましたが、アメリカ国民になったことは、私の人生の中で最大の贈り物であり、最も誇りに思う瞬間の 1 つです。 NVIDIA は私の生涯の仕事です。同僚とともにそれを今日の会社に築き上げることができたのは特権であり、光栄なことです。 NVIDIA のような企業が設立できるのはアメリカ以外にありません。私は我が国を愛していますし、NVIDIA も愛しています。
私は NVIDIA の全員が期待する基準を満たしておらず、私生活でも重大な間違いを犯しました。私は取締役会に問題を引き起こしてしまい、深く後悔しています。私は自分の間違いを完全に認めており、理事会の独立した調査に協力するつもりです。
私が退職して以来、NVIDIA の従業員、投資家、ビジネス パートナー、顧客から、CEO としての復帰を求める声が殺到しています。同社が複雑なテクノロジー、市場、競争、地政学的な力学を乗り越える中、多くの人が私に直接連絡を取り続けています。 NVIDIA は一世代に一度の企業です。私の復帰が株主、従業員、会社、そしてアメリカにとって最善であると取締役会が判断した場合、私は光栄にもこれらの呼びかけに応え、C として復帰するつもりです。

FDIC INSURANCE IS $250,000 PER BANK, PER OWNERSHIP CATEGORY
FDIC deposit insurance covers $250,000 per depositor, per FDIC-insured bank, for each account ownership category.
The limit is per bank. A single account at one insured bank and another single account at a different insured bank are each insured up to $250,000. That is up to $500,000 across the two.
It is also per category. An IRA at the same bank is separately insured up to $250,000.
Covered: checking, savings, money market deposit accounts, CDs.
Not covered: stocks, bonds, mutual funds, crypto assets.
Since the FDIC was founded in 1933, no depositor has lost a penny of FDIC-insured funds, per the FDIC.
items.title_ja:
FDIC 保険は、銀行ごと、所有権カテゴリごとに 250,000 ドルです
FDIC 預金保険は、FDIC の保険対象銀行ごとに、口座所有者のカテゴリーごとに、預金者 1 人あたり 250,000 ドルを補償します。
制限は銀行ごとにあります。ある被保険銀行の 1 つの口座と、別の被保険銀行の 1 つの口座には、それぞれ最大 250,000 ドルの保険が適用されます。 2つ合わせると最大50万ドルになります。
それもカテゴリーごとです。同じ銀行の IRA には、最大 250,000 ドルまで別途保険がかけられます。
対象: 当座預金、短期金融市場預金口座、CD。
対象外: 株式、債券、投資信託、暗号資産。
FDICによると、FDICが1933年に設立されて以来、FDICが保証する資金を一銭も失った預金者はいないという。
